title: Fork a project or clone it
summary: A fork is a hosted repository linked to an upstream project. A clone is a local repository copy. A fork can hold proposed contributions without granting write access to upstream.
introduction: A fork is a hosted repository linked to an upstream project. A clone is a local repository copy. A fork can hold proposed contributions without granting write access to upstream. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain fork a project or clone it
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A fork is a hosted repository linked to an upstream project. A clone is a local repository copy. A fork can hold proposed contributions without granting write access to upstream.

blocks.code:
Upstream project -> your hosted fork
Hosted fork -> local clone
Local commits -> proposed change from the fork
blocks.title: Fork a project or clone it

blocks.text: The fork lives on GitHub and the clone lives on a computer. Moving commits between them requires separate Git operations.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Draw where files are edited in this flow.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Forking does not remove the original licence or give permission for every use.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
